name: Anguilla
summary: Anguilla levies no income, capital gains, dividend, inheritance, gift or wealth tax on individuals. Indirect taxes changed on 1 August 2025 (9% goods tax on imports, 13% general services tax). Real estate carries a 5% transfer tax and, for non-residents, licence/stamp duty up to 12.5%.

regimes.name: Ordinary residence
regimes.description: Anguilla is a zero-direct-tax jurisdiction: no income, capital gains, estate or other direct tax on individuals.
regimes.eligibility: Any lawful resident; non-belongers need a residence permit.

capital_gains.rate_basis: No direct taxation on individuals (Deloitte Anguilla 2026).
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Real property transfer tax 5% (seller). Non-resident buyers need an alien landholding licence and pay stamp duty of up to 12.5% of the freehold value.

dividends.summary: No tax on dividends; no withholding taxes.
dividends.treaty_network: No tax treaties: US/EU withholding on portfolio dividends is not reduced.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Property tax 0.3% of value for residential buildings (0.325% short-term rental, 0.35% commercial); minimum XCD 250.

inheritance.important_exceptions: Stamp duty 0.01%-5% on documents may apply to some transfers.

residency.tax_residency_test: No direct taxes, so tax residence has no local consequence.

routes.name: Residence permit
routes.requirements: Non-belongers need permission to reside; programmes and amounts not researched.

corporate.summary: No corporate income tax; no withholding taxes; no Pillar Two commitment. Licensed financial institutions pay a 0.3% annual levy on total assets.

intl_school_annual_fee.description: Omololu International School (private, K-11), international-student tuition for secondary Grades 7-11: USD 900 a month for 10 months, USD 9,000 a year (domestic students USD 7,500), plus a USD 500 registration fee. The school teaches only to Grade 11; there is no international school offering upper-secondary/IB years on Anguilla. The page gives no school year; recorded as current at 15 Oct 2026.

cost_of_living.notes: Rent rests on one 4-bedroom long-let listing (Axarealtor); most other Anguilla agencies quote nightly holiday rates. Purchase price per m2, health insurance and housekeeper not sourced.

prime_rent_monthly.description: Single listing: a fully furnished 4-bedroom, 4-bathroom villa on two acres at Sile Bay offered by Axarealtor (South Hill) for long or short-term rental at USD 4,000 a month (negotiable; nightly rate USD 300), rent including water, internet and grounds maintenance, tenant pays electricity; read 15 Oct 2026 (the page may mark it as rented). The only 4+ bedroom home with a monthly long-let rate found on Anguilla. For context, the same page lists 3-bedroom houses at USD 2,000-3,300 a month (Shoal Bay, West End) and a new 3-bedroom West End house at USD 8,500. Very thin sample; listing undated.

us_citizen_notes: US citizens remain subject to US federal income, estate and gift tax on worldwide income and assets wherever they live; the app adds the federal layer. There is no local tax here to credit against US tax on portfolio income, so a US family pays the full US rates. No Puerto Rico-style exclusion applies.
open_questions: Not present in some World Bank/WGI datasets; no official homicide statistic was sourced for an indicator override (web-search budget exhausted).

No official, same-definition values found for homicides per 100,000, life expectancy at birth or internet use: the Anguilla Statistics Department publishes life expectancy only from the 2001 census and deaths by cause only to 2013; Royal Anguilla Police Force crime statistics were not reachable. These indicators remain missing rather than proxied from the UK.

Prime rent rests on a single 4-bedroom long-let listing (Axarealtor, Sile Bay, USD 4,000/month, 15 Oct 2026); a larger sample of monthly long-let rates for 4-5 bedroom homes (e.g. West End/Meads Bay) is needed.

source.title: World Bank Worldwide Governance Indicators: Voice and Accountability, estimate (GOV_WGI_VA.EST), Anguilla

wgi_va.notes: Same WGI series the pipeline uses. The World Bank API returns Anguilla's row with an empty ISO3 code, so the automatic fetch (keyed on ISO3) drops it; value copied from the API as is. Anguilla's estimate rests on few underlying sources, so its margin of error is wide. Latest available year is 2017 (no later Voice and Accountability estimate).
